own.bio: Strange but true stories, told quietly. New odd hour, every week.

posts.caption: In 2021, one engineer typed one wrong command and 3.5 billion people lost the internet in a single instant. Not hacked. Not attacked. Just one wrong line of code during a routine maintenance check. Facebook's own engineers couldn't even log in to fix it, their access tools were on the same servers that just vanished. They had to physically drive to data centers and override servers by hand. One by one. 6 hours. $60 million lost every single hour. And the exact same vulnerability? Still exists right now. The internet is more fragile than you think.

2021 mein ek engineer ne ek galat command type ki aur 3.5 billion logon ka internet ek pal mein band ho gaya. Hack nahi hua. Attack nahi hua. Bas ek routine maintenance check ke dauran ek galat line of code. 6 ghante. Har ghante 60 million dollar ka nuksaan. Internet utna strong nahi jitna hum sochte hain.

There is a sound that only 2% of people can hear. Scientists have studied it for 50 years and still have no answer. It's called The Hum — and the leading theory is that it's the Earth itself vibrating at a frequency most humans aren't built to detect. A woman heard it for 11 years, moved across the country to escape it, and it followed her to the new house. Stop right now, close your eyes, and listen. What do you hear?

We call space the final frontier. But we've barely explored our own planet. Earth is stranger than anything we've found out there — and most people have no idea. From perfect solar eclipses to oceans deeper than mountains are tall, this is the planet you thought you knew.

In 1974, a man calculated the exact day he would die and spent a year preparing for it. What happened next is stranger than the prediction itself. Frank was obsessed with numerology. He told his family, quit his job, and gave away everything he owned. When the day came and went without incident, he thought he'd beaten fate. He hadn't.

recentPosts.caption: In Renaissance Europe, science was being transformed into a practice anyone could participate in and even enjoy. The field of astronomy grew rapidly as new instruments were crafted to make discoveries, as you can see on the August page of our 12,026 Human Era calendar. That is when champions like Tycho Brahe, an eccentric man with a metal nose, achieved notoriety by throwing astronomy parties and collecting great volumes of star data that we still use today.

Take a journey through the cosmos with us: Explore the vastness of our Solar System, the Milky Way, and beyond. From the Oort cloud to the Laniakea Supercluster, discover just how tiny we are in the grand scheme of the universe.

YouTube’s AI Detection Kicked Us in the Face

Every creator's worst nightmare just happened to us: The YouTube algorithm actually blocked us. It started slowly at first. Some videos started showing strange view fluctuations. Our second to last video did very badly, but this just happens sometimes, so we didn’t think that much about it. 

But then our last video, about Superpredators, did *extremely* badly. It was our worst upload since 2013. But it did badly in a weird way: Almost every single m

Your brain peaked at birth. Babies may seem helpless, but their brains are incredible learning machines. They can hear sounds from any language, recognize faces adults can't, and build millions of neural connections every second!

Someone should reach out to Barbie, we might have found the pinkest asteroid out there!

Are you ready for your space adventure? Star Birds, a game we developed together with our friends at @toukana_interactive, is available on Steam!
Moon dust is no joke: it floats, clings, and cuts like glass. Each landing sends deadly particles flying through space and scientists are still scrambling for fixes.
And here we thought spiders and insects are Australia's biggest threat... 😬

Back in 1932, Australia went to war against the most unusual enemy. It wasn't another country or an invading army. It was a flock of 20,000 emus! They invaded and devastated farmers' wheat fields and the government had no other option but to take out the big guns, literally. What followed has since become one of the strangest military operations in the history: the Great Emu War.

Watch our latest Nightshift video to find out what actually happened during the Emu War, how one of the world's larg
It seems that Midas have stumbled over a rock and fell on the ground. Surely nothing bad can come out of that... 👀

On the vast, cold seas with endless waves in all directions, there is one constant companion: the stars. Whenever they were visible, sailors knew they could find their way. Their guidance meant ships could dare to cross the oceans with nothing more than keen eyesight and the ability to read the signs in the sky. Just like the brave sailors aboard Chinese junks that can be seen on the July page of our 12,026 Human Era calendar, who left familiar shores to cross oceans and head into the unknown.

War costs far more than weapons and destroyed buildings. It leaves countries poorer, disrupts education, drives migration, and passes trauma to future generations. Some of its highest costs are paid decades later.
If you don't know, don't worry! You'll find out soon on our Nightshift channel... 🌚

recentPosts.caption:
Indonesia is home to some truly incredible natural wonders. ⁠
This is the breathtaking Paisupok Lake, known for its clear waters and stunning tropical surroundings.⁠
⁠
Have you visited this hidden paradise yet? 🌴💙⁠
⁠
🎥: @mickwagey

For nearly 500 years, the Forbidden City was the center of China’s imperial power.⁠
⁠
Located in the heart of Beijing, this enormous palace complex was home to 24 emperors from the Ming and Qing dynasties, with thousands of rooms, courtyards, and historic halls hidden behind its red walls.⁠
⁠
Once closed to ordinary people, it is now open to visitors as the Palace Museum, allowing travelers to walk through the same spaces that once belonged only to China’s imperial family.⁠
⁠
By: @da_na_yang_  @

Located in Australia’s Northern Territory, this massive sandstone monolith has stood in the Outback for more than 550 million years.⁠
⁠⁠
Beyond its incredible appearance, Uluru holds deep cultural meaning for the Anangu people, its traditional owners, who have cared for this sacred place for generations.⁠
⁠
By: @tmckphotos @the.jham⁠

@passportarchives showed us one of Florida’s most iconic drives. 🌊☀️⁠
The Seven Mile Bridge, completed in 1987, connects Knight’s Key in Marathon to Little Duck Key in the Florida Keys. ⁠
⁠
Stretching across clear waters, it offers incredible ocean views and a glimpse of the historic Old Seven Mile Bridge alongside it. Definitely a destination worth adding to your Florida bucket list!

Reaching this monastery is part of the experience itself. ⁠
⁠
Paro Taktsang, also known as Tiger’s Nest Monastery, sits on a cliffside high above Bhutan’s Paro Valley.⁠
⁠
To get there, visitors follow a mountain trail through the forest before reaching one of the country’s most sacred sites, built around a cave where Guru Rinpoche is believed to have meditated.⁠
⁠
By: Rabea Brok, Karen W Lim, Sujan Mongar

Ziplining through the Swiss Alps? Hell yeah. ⁠
@sheanewkirk showed us one of the most thrilling ways to experience Switzerland’s incredible mountain landscapes.⁠
⁠
Would you try this adventure?

Burano is one of the most colorful islands in Italy, with rows of brightly painted homes lining the canals of the Venetian Lagoon.⁠
⁠
The tradition comes from the island’s fishing heritage, with local legends saying the vibrant colors helped fishermen recognize their homes when returning through the fog.⁠
⁠
Beyond its colorful streets, Burano is also known for its handmade lace, a craft that has been part of the island’s identity for centuries.⁠
⁠
By: Babar Rehman, @francesco_sgura

Summer days in Bern look like this.⁠
Thanks to @irgendwoundsatt for showing us a unique way to enjoy this beautiful city.

Kasbah Oulad Othmane in Morocco's Drâa Valley offers the chance to stay inside a beautifully restored historic fortress without spending a fortune.⁠
⁠
The kasbah combines centuries-old architecture with peaceful courtyards, rooftop views, and a glimpse into traditional Moroccan life.⁠
⁠
With rooms starting at around $45 per night, it's one of those rare places where history, scenery, and affordability come together, making it an unforgettable stop if you’re planning on exploring southern Morocco

The corpse flower in the flesh! ⁠
The largest individual flower in the world, found only in Sumatra and Borneo.⁠
Thank you, @trevtravels for sharing this incredible footage.

The temple is home to more than 1,200 stone statues, each carved with its own expression and personality. Some smile, some laugh, and no two look exactly the same.⁠
⁠
Many of the figures were carved by visitors under the guidance of sculptor Kocho Nishimura, which makes the temple feel even more personal.⁠
⁠
If you’re visiting Kyoto and want to escape the crowds for a while, this is one place worth adding to your itinerary.⁠
⁠
By: @julias_torten @daniel.gilhooley @oldisthenewgold_ @mavimiro @liu

Located in northern Laos, the Xieng Khouang Plateau is home to one of the world's most puzzling archaeological sites: the Plain of Jars.

The name comes from the hundreds of stone “jars” scattered around the area. For nearly a century, archaeologists have pondered their purpose, suspecting they were funerary urns, as some had been found with burnt bones and ashes. Have you ever seen an organism made of glass? They're called diatoms, single-celled algae encased in silica. National Geographic Explorer @arielwaldman recovered her samples of these organisms from Antarctica, but they can be found around the world—and a microscope isn't the way to see them.

Photos by @joelsartore | Active during the day, collared owlets are often seen perched high up in trees, surveilling for their next meal. These birds are on the lookout for smaller birds, which make up the majority of their diet, along with mice, lizards, and large insects. Always up for a challenge, the collared owlet has been known to take birds nearly its own size as prey when the opportunity arises. These photos were taken @fonghuanggupark. Since the 1500s, legends have spread of rat kings—writhing masses of rodents with entangled tails. Some stories say these creatures are led by one rat with psychological powers, while others claim they move together like an amalgamated monster.

It turns out they might be real, and very gruesome, but how they form remains a mystery. Learn more about rat kings at the link in bio. 🐀

Photograph by Oleksandr Rupeta, Alamy Stock Photo

The story of Pompeii, frozen in time for almost 2,000 years, has captivated people for centuries. Actor Tom Hiddleston is one of them. In the National Geographic series Pompeii: Out of Time, Hiddleston and a team of experts trace three real-life residents who were there when disaster struck—ordinary people swept up in an event that would resonate throughout history.

Read more about how Hiddleston is exploring the stories of Pompeii from a new angle at the link in bio.

#PompeiiOutOfTime with To

Some of the world’s oldest landscapes are changing before our eyes. #TimeandWater follows renowned Icelandic author Andri Snær Magnason as he reflects on the fragile beauty of a world that’s changing faster than ever. Now streaming on @disneyplus and @hulu.

Photographer @amytoensing's image of two widows at a shelter in Vrindavan, India—often called the "city of widows"—reflects a changing reality for some of the country's women. Lalita, right, bears the cropped hair and white wrap once considered obligatory for widowhood, but shelter manager Ranjana is less constrained by traditional customs. While the loss of a husband has historically brought exile and mistreatment for many, some are pushing back against the expectations placed upon them.

With a tuxedo-like appearance, its wings spread and head held high, this Adélie penguin presents a dapper figure as it waddles through an Antarctic colony. These penguins have been known to dive as deep as 575 feet 9175 meters) in search of food. 

Photograph by George F. Mobley

Raccoons are found in most US cities, environments that were built for humans but allow raccoons to thrive. While most will never achieve the worldwide fame of internet fave Jimothy, these clever urban icons and their problem-solving skills are still fascinating to both scientists and the public alike.

Learn more about urban raccoons at the link in bio.

Photographs by Corey Arnold @arni_coraldo

Retiring at 100 years old? Not a chance! Here’s a sneak peek of Sir David Attenborough working on the narration for the upcoming BLUE PLANET III.

#DavidAttenborough100 #DavidAttenborough #BluePlanetIII

When the midnight cravings hit 🌙
 
As night falls across the Namib desert, a desert rain frog emerges from beneath the sand in search of food. With only a few hours before temperatures begin to rise, it must make the most of the cooler conditions to find enough food for itself.
 
Explore the world’s few remaining untouched landscapes with Eden: Untamed Planet. Find the full series via the link in our bio 🔗

#EdenUntamedPlanet #DesertRainFrog #NightHunt #Namib

One of the most extraordinary transformations in evolution 🦌🐋

Millions of years ago, some mammals returned to the water. And over generations they became more streamlined and limbs turned to flippers, making them aquatic marvels. 

Find out where to watch Evolution via the link in our bio 🔗💚

#Evolution #ChrisPackham #Nature

You are what you eat 🍽️

Roseate spoonbills have a diet that is thought to give them their pink plumage. Shrimps, crabs and crayfish contain organic pigments called carotenoids that changes their feather colour when eaten.

#EarthCapture by @batzellapaola
.
.
.
.
#RoseateSpoonbill #Wildlife #Nature

Didn’t see that coming 👀
 
Perfectly hidden beneath the mud and vegetation, a mugger crocodile waits as a thirsty chital deer approaches the water’s edge. In a split second, it launches from its hiding place, but will the deer manage to escape? 
 
Celebrate 20 years of Planet Earth with us. Find out where to watch the full episode via our link in bio 💚

#PlanetEarth #DavidAttenborough #PE20 #PEIII

Nature never fails to surprise us 🌍

Discover 20 unforgettable Planet Earth moments that prove the natural world is stranger, smarter and more spectacular than we can ever imagine. 

Head over to the link in our bio to read the full article 🔗

#PlanetEarth #ExtraordinaryAnimals #PE20

Is the anus an underrated innovation? 🍑

Mutations in an ancestor called the urbilaterian lengthened their bodies over generations. A tube formed with a mouth for eating and an anus for pooing. This was a breakthrough invention creating the one-way through-gut for continuous feeding.

Find out where to watch Evolution via the link in our bio 🔗💚

#Evolution #ChrisPackham #Nature

A mouthful of teeth 🦁🦷

30 to be precise. As predators and carnivores, lions use their teeth to hunt and eat. They have twelve incisors, four canines, ten premolars and four molars for gripping prey and cutting meat.

#EarthCapture by @jackswynnerton
.
.
.
.
#Lion #Wildlife #Nature

Waiting for the perfect moment 🐆
 
Perched high above the ground, the leopard waits until an impala comes within striking distance. After staying completely still, it launches from the tree in one powerful leap, but will all that patience pay off?
 
Celebrate 20 years of Planet Earth with us. Find out where to watch the full episode via our link in bio 💚

#PlanetEarth #DavidAttenborough #PE20 #PEIII

How do you attract a female? 🦌🦕

The most attractive are usually the biggest and hairiest with prominent features. In reproduction, they pass their genes to the next generation, who inherit more exaggerated attributes. Over millions of years, animal traits modify for better mating chances.

Find out where to watch Evolution via the link in our bio 🔗💚

#Evolution #ChrisPackham #Nature

Someone’s got serious aim 🎯
 
An archerfish doesn’t chase its prey. Instead, it fires a powerful jet of water with remarkable precision, knocking unsuspecting insects straight into the water. One perfectly placed shot is all it takes before the fish darts in to claim its meal. 
 
Celebrate 20 years of Planet Earth with us. Find out where to watch the full episode via our link in bio 💚

#PlanetEarth #DavidAttenborough #PE20 #PEIII

Penises come in all shapes and sizes 🍆

Shells prevented reptiles from fertilising their eggs, yet evolution created a solution: the penis. Reptiles were among the first animals to have them, but they weren’t the last. For life on land, it meant sex as we know it had been invented.

Find out where to watch Evolution via the link in our bio 🔗💚

#Evolution #ChrisPackham #Nature
